title: Invariant coefficient sections
statement: Let $V$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\ell\in\mathbb N$, $P$ a finite group and $c:Y\to V$ a finite etale $\operatorname{ULift}(P)$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Write $E_c$ for its equivariant locally constant section presheaf functor [def-weil-pbc-torsor-associated-module], and $S$ for restriction of scalars along $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbb Z/\ell)\to\mathbb Z/\ell$. The presheaf $S E_c$ of the trivial representation on $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbb Z/\ell)$ is isomorphic to the underlying presheaf of the constant coefficient sheaf on $V$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The maps are descent of invariant functions and pullback to the torsor.

proof.text: Construct the natural linear map from the constant coefficient presheaf to invariant sections by constant functions. It is locally injective: equality can be evaluated at a lift of any point along the surjective pullback of the torsor. If distinct coefficients have equal images, the base object is empty and the empty covering witnesses local equality.

For an invariant section s over W, cover W times_V c.P by the open fibers U_a of s, regarded as etale objects over c.P and hence over V. Their maps to W jointly cover W because the torsor projection is surjective. On U_a, evaluate both the restricted invariant section and the constant coefficient a on the graph U_a to c.P. The graph followed by section restriction is the inclusion U_a to W times_V c.P, so both evaluations equal a. The injective half of diagonalEvaluation_bijective proves equality of the sections. This proves local surjectivity without a global function-descent theorem.

The restricted equivariant presheaf is a sheaf by equivariantModulePresheaf_isSheaf. Lift the constant-to-invariant map along sheafification. Mathlib toSheafify_sheafifyLift and Presheaf.comp_isLocallyInjective_iff / comp_isLocallySurjective_iff transfer local bijectivity to this lift. Apply Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso, then pass to underlying presheaves and reverse the isomorphism.
